items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: conservative

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Early estimates of the damage turned out to be far too ______; the true cost was almost three times higher."

explanation.en: A "conservative" estimate is cautiously low, which fits a figure that turned out to be much lower than the true cost. "Exaggerated" and "excessive" mean too high, the opposite, and "precise" contradicts the large error.
explanation.th: conservative estimate คือการประมาณการแบบระมัดระวังซึ่งมักต่ำกว่าความจริง ตรงกับที่ค่าเสียหายจริงสูงกว่าเกือบสามเท่า ส่วน exaggerated และ excessive แปลว่าสูงเกินไป (ตรงข้าม) และ precise ขัดกับความคลาดเคลื่อนที่มาก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: acceptance

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำนาม

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The theory was initially dismissed, but it has since gained wide ______ among geologists."

explanation.en: "Gain wide acceptance" is a fixed collocation meaning that many people come to believe something, which contrasts with "initially dismissed". The other nouns do not collocate with "gain wide … among".
explanation.th: gain wide acceptance เป็นคำปรากฏร่วมที่แปลว่า ได้รับการยอมรับอย่างกว้างขวาง ตรงข้ามกับ initially dismissed ส่วนคำนามอื่นใช้กับโครงสร้างนี้ไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: curb

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The government plans to ______ the use of single-use plastic bags by charging customers for each one."

explanation.en: To "curb" something is to limit or control it; charging for bags is a way to reduce their use. "Promote" and "accelerate" would increase use, and "compile" means collect information.
explanation.th: curb แปลว่า ควบคุม จำกัด การเก็บเงินค่าถุงเป็นวิธีลดการใช้ ส่วน promote และ accelerate จะทำให้ใช้มากขึ้น และ compile แปลว่า รวบรวมข้อมูล

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: contradictory

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The two studies reached ______ conclusions: one found the drug effective, while the other found no benefit at all."

explanation.en: One study found benefit and the other none, so the conclusions were "contradictory" (opposed to each other). "Complementary" and "consistent" suggest they agree or fit together; "comprehensive" means thorough.
explanation.th: งานหนึ่งพบว่ายาได้ผล อีกงานไม่พบประโยชน์ ข้อสรุปจึง contradictory (ขัดแย้งกัน) ส่วน complementary และ consistent สื่อว่าสอดคล้องเสริมกัน และ comprehensive แปลว่า ครอบคลุม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: corroborate

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Fossils of feathered dinosaurs discovered in China strongly ______ the hypothesis that birds evolved from dinosaurs."

explanation.en: Feathered dinosaurs are evidence that supports a dinosaur–bird link, so they "corroborate" (confirm) the hypothesis. "Refute" means prove wrong, "fabricate" means invent falsely and "dissipate" means scatter or disappear.
explanation.th: ฟอสซิลไดโนเสาร์ที่มีขนเป็นหลักฐานสนับสนุนว่านกวิวัฒนาการจากไดโนเสาร์ จึงใช้ corroborate (ยืนยัน) ส่วน refute = หักล้าง, fabricate = กุขึ้น, dissipate = สลายไป

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: vague

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Because the instructions were so ______, almost every participant interpreted them differently."

explanation.en: Different interpretations result from unclear instructions, so "vague" fits. "Lucid" means clear, "meticulous" means very careful and detailed, and "rigid" means strict; none would cause confusion.
explanation.th: การตีความต่างกันเกิดจากคำสั่งที่ไม่ชัดเจน จึงใช้ vague ส่วน lucid = ชัดเจน, meticulous = ละเอียดรอบคอบ, rigid = เข้มงวด ไม่ทำให้สับสน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: driven

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำกริยา

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The company's profits fell sharply, ______ largely by rising energy costs and weak demand."

explanation.en: "Driven by" means caused by: the fall in profits was caused by costs and weak demand. "Derived" takes "from", "deprived" takes "of", and "deterred" (discouraged) needs a person or action as its object.
explanation.th: driven by แปลว่า เกิดจาก/ขับเคลื่อนโดย กำไรลดลงเพราะต้นทุนและอุปสงค์ต่ำ ส่วน derived ใช้กับ from, deprived ใช้กับ of และ deterred แปลว่า ยับยั้งไม่ให้ทำ

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: deliberately

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Unlike earlier tools, which were made from whatever stone was at hand, these axes were made from rock that had been ______ selected for its hardness."

explanation.en: Selecting rock "for its hardness" shows intention, in contrast with "whatever stone was at hand", so "deliberately" (on purpose) fits. "Accidentally" is the opposite, and "reluctantly" and "scarcely" make no sense here.
explanation.th: การเลือกหินเพราะความแข็งแสดงความตั้งใจ ตรงข้ามกับการใช้หินอะไรก็ได้ที่หาได้ จึงใช้ deliberately (โดยเจตนา) ส่วน accidentally ตรงข้าม และ reluctantly, scarcely ไม่เข้ากับความหมาย

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: impasse

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำนาม

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"The negotiations reached an ______: neither side was willing to make further concessions."

explanation.en: An "impasse" is a situation in which no progress is possible, which is explained by "neither side was willing to make further concessions". An "agreement" is the opposite, "outcome" is too general to match the explanation, and an "ultimatum" is a final demand made by one side.
explanation.th: impasse คือ ทางตัน ไม่มีความคืบหน้า ซึ่งอธิบายด้วยข้อความว่าไม่มีฝ่ายใดยอมอ่อนข้อ ส่วน agreement (ข้อตกลง) ตรงข้าม, outcome กว้างเกินไป และ ultimatum คือคำขาดจากฝ่ายเดียว

items.subject: eng

skill.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการในบริบท: pertinent

topic.th: คำศัพท์วิชาการ: คำคุณศัพท์และคำวิเศษณ์

items.stem:
Choose the word or phrase that best completes the sentence.
"Her comments were highly ______ to the debate: they addressed the central question directly."

explanation.en: "Pertinent" means directly relevant, as the second clause explains. "Peripheral" means of minor importance or at the edge, the opposite; "permanent" and "persistent" do not take "to the debate" in this sense.
explanation.th: pertinent แปลว่า ตรงประเด็น ตามที่ประโยคหลังอธิบาย ส่วน peripheral = อยู่ชายขอบ ไม่สำคัญ (ตรงข้าม) และ permanent, persistent ไม่มีความหมายนี้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: วลี V3 บอกเหตุผล (ความรู้สึก)

topic.th: อนุประโยคลดรูปและวลี participle

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"______ by the speed of the results, the team decided to repeat the experiment."

explanation.en: The team was surprised (passive feeling), so the participle clause uses "Surprised by …". "Surprising" and "Having surprised" would mean the team surprised someone else, and "To surprise" expresses purpose.
explanation.th: ทีมรู้สึกประหลาดใจ (ถูกทำให้แปลกใจ) จึงใช้ Surprised by ส่วน Surprising และ Having surprised หมายถึงทีมทำให้คนอื่นแปลกใจ และ To surprise บอกจุดประสงค์

items.subject: eng

skill.th: subjunctive หลัง recommend

topic.th: subjunctive และประโยคเงื่อนไข

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The report recommends that the factory ______ its emissions by half within five years."

explanation.en: After "recommend that", formal English uses the subjunctive base form for every subject: "the factory reduce". "Reduces" and "will reduce" are ordinary indicative forms, and "reducing" is not a finite verb.
explanation.th: หลัง recommend that ในภาษาทางการใช้ subjunctive คือกริยารูปพื้นฐานเสมอ จึงเป็น the factory reduce ส่วน reduces และ will reduce เป็นรูปปกติ และ reducing เป็นกริยาแท้ไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: inversion หลัง Seldom

topic.th: การสลับที่ประธานกับกริยา (inversion)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"Seldom ______ such a rapid decline in a bird population."

explanation.en: Negative adverbs such as "Seldom" at the start of a sentence require auxiliary + subject: "have ecologists observed". The normal word order is wrong after a fronted "Seldom".
explanation.th: คำวิเศษณ์เชิงปฏิเสธอย่าง Seldom ที่ขึ้นต้นประโยค ต้องเรียงเป็น กริยาช่วย + ประธาน คือ have ecologists observed การเรียงแบบปกติจึงผิด

items.subject: eng

skill.th: noun clause คู่ขนานกับ not ... but

topic.th: noun clause (อนุประโยคนาม)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The problem is not that the data are wrong but ______."

explanation.en: "Not … but" must join parallel elements. The first is a noun clause "that the data are wrong", so the second must be a noun clause too: "that they have been misinterpreted" (the data are misinterpreted by people, so passive).
explanation.th: not ... but ต้องเชื่อมสิ่งที่ขนานกัน ส่วนแรกเป็น noun clause (that the data are wrong) ส่วนที่สองจึงต้องเป็น noun clause เช่นกัน คือ that they have been misinterpreted และต้องเป็น passive เพราะข้อมูลถูกตีความผิด

items.subject: eng

skill.th: โครงสร้างคู่ขนานกับ not only ... but also

topic.th: โครงสร้างคู่ขนาน (parallelism)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"Effective science communication requires not only accuracy but also ______."

explanation.en: "Not only accuracy" is a noun, so "but also" must be followed by a noun: "clarity". The infinitive, the -ing phrase and the clause are not parallel.
explanation.th: หลัง not only เป็นคำนาม accuracy ดังนั้นหลัง but also ต้องเป็นคำนามเช่นกัน คือ clarity ส่วน to-infinitive, วลี -ing และอนุประโยคไม่ขนานกัน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: appositive (นามวลีขยายนาม)

topic.th: appositive และ relative clause

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The Silk Road, ______, carried ideas and religions as well as goods."
choices: it linked China with the Mediterranean
a network of trade routes linking China with the Mediterranean
was a network of trade routes linking China with the Mediterranean
which a network of trade routes linking China with the Mediterranean

explanation.en: Between the commas we need a noun phrase renaming the Silk Road: "a network of trade routes linking China with the Mediterranean". "Which" needs a verb, and the choices with "was" or "it linked" add a second clause without a connector.
explanation.th: ระหว่างจุลภาคต้องเป็นนามวลีที่อธิบาย The Silk Road ส่วน which ต้องมีกริยาตาม และแบบที่มี was หรือ it linked ทำให้มีประโยคซ้อนโดยไม่มีคำเชื่อม

items.subject: eng

skill.th: relative clause ลดรูปแบบ passive

topic.th: อนุประโยคลดรูปและวลี participle

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The bridge, ______ in less than two years, was considered an engineering marvel at the time."

explanation.en: "Completed" is the reduced form of "which was completed": the bridge was completed by builders. "Completing" is active, "was completed" would give the sentence two main verbs, and "having completing" is not a correct form.
explanation.th: completed คือรูปลดของ which was completed เพราะสะพานถูกสร้างเสร็จ ส่วน completing เป็น active, was completed ทำให้มีกริยาแท้สองตัว และ having completing ผิดรูป

items.subject: eng

skill.th: หลีกเลี่ยงส่วนขยายลอย

topic.th: ส่วนขยายลอย (dangling modifier)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"Written in plain language, ______."
choices: readers with no scientific training can understand the guide
the guide can be understood by readers with no scientific training
it is easy for readers to understand the guide
we found that the guide was easy to understand

explanation.en: What is "written in plain language" is the guide, so the guide must be the subject of the main clause: "the guide can be understood by readers …". The other choices make readers, "it" or "we" the thing that was written.
explanation.th: สิ่งที่ถูกเขียนด้วยภาษาง่ายคือคู่มือ ประธานของประโยคหลักจึงต้องเป็น the guide ส่วนแบบอื่นทำให้ readers, it หรือ we กลายเป็นสิ่งที่ถูกเขียน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: noun clause แบบ whether ... or

topic.th: noun clause (อนุประโยคนาม)

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"It is still debated ______ the ancient city was abandoned suddenly or declined over many decades."

explanation.en: The clause presents two alternatives ("suddenly or … over many decades"), so "whether … or" is needed. "That" states a fact rather than an open question, "what" needs a gap in the clause, and "if or not" is not standard.
explanation.th: อนุประโยคเสนอทางเลือกสองทาง จึงต้องใช้ whether ... or ส่วน that ทำให้เป็นข้อเท็จจริงแทนคำถาม what ต้องมีช่องว่างในอนุประโยค และ if or not ไม่ใช่รูปมาตรฐาน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: inversion ในเงื่อนไขแบบที่ 3

topic.th: subjunctive และประโยคเงื่อนไข

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"______ the warning signs earlier, the disease could have been controlled."

explanation.en: The result "could have been controlled" refers to the past, so the condition must be past perfect. Without "if", the auxiliary moves to the front: "Had doctors recognised". "If doctors recognised" is the wrong tense, and the other two are not correct conditional forms.
explanation.th: ผลลัพธ์ could have been controlled เป็นอดีต เงื่อนไขจึงต้องเป็น past perfect และเมื่อละ if ต้องนำ Had ขึ้นหน้า คือ Had doctors recognised ส่วน If doctors recognised ผิดกาล และอีกสองแบบไม่ใช่รูปเงื่อนไขที่ถูก

items.subject: eng

skill.th: ความสอดคล้องของกริยาใน relative clause

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องประธาน–กริยาและการเปรียบเทียบ

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The number of species that ______ extinct in the past century is far higher than natural rates would predict."

explanation.en: The relative pronoun "that" refers to "species" (plural), so its verb is "have become"; the main verb "is" agrees with "The number". "Has become" wrongly agrees with "number", "becoming" is not finite, and "was become" is not a correct form.
explanation.th: that ในอนุประโยคแทน species (พหูพจน์) กริยาจึงเป็น have become ส่วนกริยาหลัก is สอดคล้องกับ The number ดังนั้น has become ผิดเพราะไปสอดคล้องกับ number, becoming ไม่ใช่กริยาแท้ และ was become ผิดรูป

items.subject: eng

skill.th: บุพบท + which ใน relative clause

topic.th: appositive และ relative clause

items.stem:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence.
"The extent ______ human activity influences climate is no longer seriously disputed among scientists."

explanation.en: We say "to an extent", so the relative clause is "the extent to which human activity influences climate". "Which" alone leaves the preposition out, and "in that" and "of what" cannot introduce a relative clause after "extent".
explanation.th: เราพูดว่า to an extent ดังนั้น relative clause ต้องเป็น the extent to which ส่วน which อย่างเดียวขาดบุพบท และ in that, of what ใช้ขึ้นต้น relative clause หลัง extent ไม่ได้

items.subject: eng

skill.th: despite ไม่ใช้ of

topic.th: รูปคำและการใช้คำ

items.stem:
Choose the underlined part that must be changed for the sentence to be correct.
[[Despite of]] the heavy rain, the field researchers [[managed]] to collect [[all]] the samples they [[needed]].

explanation.en: "Despite" is followed directly by a noun: "Despite the heavy rain" (or "In spite of the heavy rain"). "Despite of" is incorrect.
explanation.th: despite ตามด้วยคำนามได้ทันที คือ Despite the heavy rain หรือใช้ In spite of ส่วน Despite of ผิด

items.subject: eng

skill.en: Subject–verb agreement across a relative clause
skill.th: ประธาน–กริยาสอดคล้องแม้มี relative clause คั่น

topic.th: ความสอดคล้องประธาน–กริยาและการเปรียบเทียบ

items.stem:
Choose the underlined part that must be changed for the sentence to be correct.
The ancient manuscripts, [[which]] were discovered in a cave in 1947, [[has provided]] scholars with [[valuable]] information [[about]] early religious texts.

explanation.en: The subject is "The ancient manuscripts" (plural), so the verb must be "have provided". The relative clause between the commas does not change the subject.
explanation.th: ประธานคือ The ancient manuscripts (พหูพจน์) กริยาจึงต้องเป็น have provided อนุประโยคระหว่างจุลภาคไม่ได้เปลี่ยนประธาน

items.subject: eng

skill.th: บุพบทคงที่ similar to

topic.th: รูปคำและการใช้คำ

items.stem:
Choose the underlined part that must be changed for the sentence to be correct.
Scientists [[have long]] debated whether animals [[are capable of]] feeling emotions [[similar with]] [[those]] of humans.

explanation.en: The adjective "similar" takes "to": "similar to those of humans". "Those" correctly replaces the plural "emotions".
explanation.th: คำคุณศัพท์ similar ใช้กับ to คือ similar to those of humans ส่วน those ใช้แทน emotions ที่เป็นพหูพจน์ได้ถูกต้อง

items.subject: eng

skill.th: infinitive ที่ขนานกันหลัง forced ... to

topic.th: โครงสร้างคู่ขนาน (parallelism)

items.passage:
Wolves, Elk and a Famous Ecological Story

When grey wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone National Park in 1995 and 1996, after an absence of roughly seventy years, few people anticipated that the return of a single predator would become one of the most famous stories in modern ecology. Within a decade, scientists were reporting changes that seemed to ripple through the entire ecosystem. Elk, the wolves' main prey, had declined in number and, it was argued, changed their behaviour, avoiding the open river valleys where they were most vulnerable. Freed from constant grazing, willow and aspen trees along the riverbanks began to recover. Beavers, which depend on willow, returned to areas they had abandoned, and their dams created ponds that supported fish, amphibians and birds.

This chain of effects is an example of what ecologists call a trophic cascade: a process in which a change at the top of a food chain spreads downward through the levels below it. The Yellowstone case was quickly adopted as a powerful illustration of the importance of large predators, and it was widely used to support the argument that restoring missing species can repair damaged ecosystems, an approach often referred to as rewilding.

In recent years, however, a number of researchers have questioned whether the story is quite so simple. One difficulty is that wolves were not the only factor changing at the time. Yellowstone experienced a series of droughts, human hunting of elk outside the park increased, and populations of other predators, including bears and cougars, were also growing. Separating the influence of wolves from these other forces is extremely difficult. Another difficulty concerns the so-called "landscape of fear". Studies that tracked elk with GPS collars found that the animals did not consistently avoid risky areas in the way the original theory suggested, raising doubts about whether fear of wolves alone could explain the recovery of trees.

Critics have also pointed out that the recovery of vegetation has been patchy. In some places willows have grown tall; in others they remain short. One explanation is that the streams themselves have changed. When beavers disappeared, their dams collapsed, the water table dropped and the streams cut deeper channels. Willows growing high above the water may now be unable to reach it, regardless of how many elk are present. If so, removing a predator may cause changes that cannot be undone simply by bringing it back.

None of this means that wolves have had no effect. Most ecologists accept that they have influenced elk numbers and, through them, parts of the ecosystem. The debate is about the size and reliability of the effects. Its lesson may be that ecosystems are rarely governed by a single cause, and that compelling stories, however useful for winning public support, should not substitute for careful evidence.
items.stem: What is the main point of the passage?
choices: Wolves should not have been reintroduced to Yellowstone because they harmed the ecosystem.
Beavers, rather than wolves, are the most important animals in Yellowstone.
The widely told story of how wolves transformed Yellowstone is now considered more complicated than it first appeared.
Trophic cascades occur only in national parks with large predators.

explanation.en: The passage tells the famous trophic-cascade story and then spends three paragraphs on reasons why it is "not quite so simple". The author never says the reintroduction was harmful and states that wolves have had some effect.

Rethinking the Marshmallow Test

In a series of studies that began at Stanford University in the late 1960s, young children were offered a simple choice. A researcher placed a treat, such as a marshmallow, in front of the child and explained that she had to leave the room for a while. If the child waited until she returned, he or she would receive two treats; if not, the child could ring a bell at any time and eat the single treat immediately. Some children waited the full fifteen minutes or so; others gave in after a few seconds.

The experiment became famous because of what happened later. Follow-up studies, published in the late 1980s and 1990s, reported that children who had waited longer tended, as adolescents, to have higher test scores, to cope better with stress, and to be rated by their parents as more competent. The conclusion seemed clear and appealing: the ability to delay gratification is a stable personal trait that appears early in life and predicts success. The "marshmallow test" entered popular culture, and books, parenting guides and school programmes urged adults to train children's willpower.

Yet the original follow-up samples were small and unusual. Most of the children were the sons and daughters of staff and students at an elite university. In 2018 a team of researchers attempted to repeat the key finding with a much larger and more varied group of more than 900 children. They did find a link between waiting time and later academic achievement, but it was about half the size of the original estimate. More importantly, once they took into account factors such as family income, the mother's education and the child's early cognitive ability, the link became very small indeed.

This result suggests a different interpretation. Children's decisions to wait may reflect not only their self-control but also their circumstances. A child who has grown up in an environment where promises are reliably kept has good reason to believe that a second marshmallow will really arrive. A child whose experience has taught that resources can disappear may quite reasonably take what is available now. Other experiments support this view: when children were first exposed to an adult who broke a small promise, they waited far less time than children whose adult had kept it.

It would be wrong to conclude that self-control does not matter. The newer findings, however, cast doubt on the idea that a few minutes of behaviour in a laboratory reveal a fixed quality of character. They also suggest that efforts to improve children's lives may achieve more by making their environments stable and trustworthy than by teaching them simply to resist temptation.

choices: explain how parents can train children to wait for rewards
argue that self-control has no influence on success
criticise Stanford University for choosing its participants unfairly
show how later research changed the interpretation of a famous experiment

explanation.en: The passage describes the original study, then a larger 2018 study and new experiments that suggest "a different interpretation". The author explicitly says it would be wrong to conclude that self-control does not matter.

Beyond the Tragedy of the Commons

In 1968 the ecologist Garrett Hardin published an essay entitled "The Tragedy of the Commons", which became one of the most cited works in the social sciences. Hardin asked his readers to imagine a pasture open to all. Each herder, acting rationally, gains the full benefit of adding one more animal to the pasture, while the cost of overgrazing is shared among everyone. As a result, each herder keeps adding animals until the pasture is ruined. "Freedom in a commons," Hardin concluded, "brings ruin to all." Since the users of a shared resource could not be expected to restrain themselves, he argued, the resource must either be divided into private property or controlled by the state.

Hardin's argument was elegant, and it seemed to explain a range of real problems, from the collapse of fisheries to air pollution. However, it rested on an assumption that the political economist Elinor Ostrom spent much of her career examining: that the users of a common resource are unable to communicate and make rules for themselves. Ostrom and her colleagues studied hundreds of cases around the world, including Swiss alpine meadows, Japanese forests, irrigation systems in Nepal and fishing grounds in Turkey. Many of these resources had been managed sustainably by local communities for generations, in some instances for centuries, without either privatisation or central control.

From these cases Ostrom identified a set of conditions that successful communities tended to share. The boundaries of the resource and the group entitled to use it were clearly defined. The people affected by the rules could take part in changing them. Users' behaviour was monitored, often by the users themselves, and those who broke the rules faced penalties that began mildly and increased for repeated offences. Disputes could be resolved quickly and cheaply, and outside authorities recognised the community's right to organise itself.

Ostrom did not claim that communities always succeed; she documented many failures as well. Nor did she reject private property or government regulation, which she regarded as suitable in some circumstances. Her objection was to the belief that any single solution could be applied everywhere. Policies imposed from outside, she found, sometimes destroyed working local arrangements and left resources worse managed than before.

In 2009 Ostrom became the first woman to receive the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences. Her work has influenced the management of resources from groundwater to the internet, and it has encouraged researchers to ask not whether shared resources are doomed, but under what conditions people manage to cooperate.

explanation.en: After presenting Hardin's pessimistic argument, the passage focuses on Ostrom's finding that communities can manage common resources and on the conditions for their success. The other statements are Hardin's view, unsupported or contradicted.

How Bacteria Outwit Antibiotics

When penicillin became widely available in the 1940s, it seemed to many that the war against bacterial infection had been won. Diseases that had killed millions could suddenly be cured in days. Yet as early as 1945, Alexander Fleming, who had discovered penicillin, warned that its misuse could make bacteria resistant to it. His warning has proved accurate. Today, infections that resist treatment with standard antibiotics are estimated to contribute to more than a million deaths each year, and health authorities regard antimicrobial resistance as one of the most serious threats to global health.

Resistance is, at its root, an example of evolution by natural selection, occurring at a speed that can be observed within a human lifetime. In any large population of bacteria, a few individuals may carry genetic differences that allow them to survive a particular antibiotic. Some produce enzymes that break the drug down; others pump it out of their cells or alter the structures it is designed to attack. When the antibiotic is used, susceptible bacteria die, but resistant ones survive and multiply. Because bacteria can reproduce every twenty minutes or so under ideal conditions, a resistant strain can become dominant remarkably quickly.

Bacteria also have a means of spreading resistance that has no close parallel in animals. Through a process known as horizontal gene transfer, they can pass small rings of DNA, called plasmids, directly to other bacteria, including bacteria of different species. A resistance gene that arises in a harmless organism living in the gut can therefore end up in a dangerous one. This explains why resistance to a new antibiotic sometimes appears in several different kinds of bacteria within a few years of the drug's introduction.

Human behaviour has greatly accelerated the process. Antibiotics are often prescribed for illnesses caused by viruses, against which they have no effect; patients sometimes stop taking them as soon as they feel better; and in many countries large quantities are given to farm animals, not to treat disease but to make them grow faster. Each of these practices exposes bacteria to antibiotics without killing all of them, creating ideal conditions for the selection of resistant strains.

Meanwhile, the development of new antibiotics has slowed dramatically. Because antibiotics are taken for short periods and new ones are held in reserve for the most serious cases, they earn far less money than medicines for long-term conditions, and many pharmaceutical companies have left the field. Experts argue that solving the problem will require action on several fronts at once: using existing drugs more carefully, improving hygiene and vaccination to prevent infections in the first place, and finding new ways to reward the development of drugs that society hopes will rarely be used.

How Bacteria Outwit Antibiotics

When penicillin became widely available in the 1940s, it seemed to many that the war against bacterial infection had been won. Diseases that had killed millions could suddenly be cured in days. Yet as early as 1945, Alexander Fleming, who had discovered penicillin, warned that its misuse could make bacteria resistant to it. His warning has proved accurate. Today, infections that resist treatment with standard antibiotics are estimated to contribute to more than a million deaths each year, and health authorities regard antimicrobial resistance as one of the most serious threats to global health.

Resistance is, at its root, an example of evolution by natural selection, occurring at a speed that can be observed within a human lifetime. In any large population of bacteria, a few individuals may carry genetic differences that allow them to survive a particular antibiotic. Some produce enzymes that break the drug down; others pump it out of their cells or alter the structures it is designed to attack. When the antibiotic is used, susceptible bacteria die, but resistant ones survive and multiply. Because bacteria can reproduce every twenty minutes or so under ideal conditions, a resistant strain can become dominant remarkably quickly.

Bacteria also have a means of spreading resistance that has no close parallel in animals. Through a process known as horizontal gene transfer, they can pass small rings of DNA, called plasmids, directly to other bacteria, including bacteria of different species. A resistance gene that arises in a harmless organism living in the gut can therefore end up in a dangerous one. This explains why resistance to a new antibiotic sometimes appears in several different kinds of bacteria within a few years of the drug's introduction.

Human behaviour has greatly accelerated the process. Antibiotics are often prescribed for illnesses caused by viruses, against which they have no effect; patients sometimes stop taking them as soon as they feel better; and in many countries large quantities are given to farm animals, not to treat disease but to make them grow faster. Each of these practices exposes bacteria to antibiotics without killing all of them, creating ideal conditions for the selection of resistant strains.

Meanwhile, the development of new antibiotics has slowed dramatically. Because antibiotics are taken for short periods and new ones are held in reserve for the most serious cases, they earn far less money than medicines for long-term conditions, and many pharmaceutical companies have left the field. Experts argue that solving the problem will require action on several fronts at once: using existing drugs more carefully, improving hygiene and vaccination to prevent infections in the first place, and finding new ways to reward the development of drugs that society hopes will rarely be used.

choices: to argue that meat should not be eaten
to explain how plasmids are transferred between species

items.stem: What can be inferred from the final paragraph about a highly effective new antibiotic?
choices: It might earn little money because doctors would try to use it only when other drugs fail.
It would earn more money than medicines for long-term conditions.
It would be immune to the development of resistance.
It would quickly replace all existing antibiotics.

explanation.en: New antibiotics are "held in reserve for the most serious cases", so they are used rarely and "earn far less money". A powerful new drug would be kept in reserve in the same way. Nothing suggests it would be free from resistance.
